Hauer, A. (2013). Thermal Energy Storage. IEA-ETSAP and IRENA Technology Policy Brief E17. https://iea-etsap.org/

NO CURRENCY YEAR is stated for any EUR figure (Table 1, pp.2 and 5-7). 2013_EUR (publication year, January 2013) is used as a flagged judgement; the cited sources ([1] Hauer 2011, [12] Hauer 2010) suggest 2010-2011 prices. The Table 8 cost block is labelled 'US$ 2008' but is not used (see source-defects).

Main file: Table 1 (body) values for sensible and phase-change storage - thermal power (capacity), round-trip storage efficiency and cost per kWh of storage capacity (COST BASIS: incremental, as an add-on store) - plus description and state of development, and the technical lifetime (10-30+ yr) from the Table 8 technical block (a separate process). Candidate archetype: thermal-storage_electric (storage side only); the brief never discusses electric charging, and Table 1 is generic across buildings, district heating and industry, with the sensible row labelled 'hot water'. Sidecars (not loaded): _thermochemical (Table 1 chemical row, the mobile zeolite waste-heat store of p.5, Table 4 reactions, CaCl2 example - NO ARCHETYPE exists for sorption/thermochemical storage); _storage-properties (energy density, storage period, store temperatures, Table 2 PCM properties, Table 7 status, Table 6 break-even costs); _out-of-scope (seasonal/district-heating and building examples); _summary-table-as-printed (Table 8 verbatim, with why each row is or is not used). Not extracted: Table 3 (sorption materials, no numbers), Table 5 (qualitative applications), European potential estimates (p.2, p.7). Store temperatures are not recorded as temperature-output because they are storage-medium temperatures, not delivered-heat temperatures.

(1) Table 8 prints the PCM cost as 'ott-50', a spreadsheet date conversion of '10-50' (Table 1 and pp.2, 6 give EUR 10-50/kWh). (2) Table 8's lower technical rows and cost block contradict the body: sizes in MWe (25 / 0.5 / 100) against Table 1's 0.001-10 MW thermal power; installed capacity of 18 GW for thermochemical storage against 5/95 market/R&D in Table 7; investment costs per kW in US$2008 that rank thermochemical storage cheapest against EUR/kWh body costs that rank it dearest; load factors and availabilities with no basis in the text. (3) Storage periods differ: Table 1 d/m, h/m, h/d vs Table 8 d-y, h-w, h-d. (4) No currency year for any EUR figure. (5) Table 1's sensible row is labelled 'hot water', but its cost range (0.1-10 EUR/kWh) is the one p.6 gives for UTES. (6) Table 6's 'Invest. cost EUR/kWh' column is a maximum affordable (break-even) cost, not a cost. (7) Table 1's column headers are rotated; the text layer splits 'Power (MW)' and loses its '('. (8) Typos: 'CA(OH)2=CAO+H2O' (Table 4), 'Aborption TES' (Table 7), 'Erytritol' (Table 2), 'encapulation' (Table 7), 'filed' for 'field' (p.7). (9) The mobile sorption store's transport distance is 'seven kilometers' in the text and '<= 10 km' in Fig. 6.
